creator: nocturne
statement: The Well (cavern 1) is resource generation and management; 10 rocks total, starting with gravel and one bucket.

creator: nocturne
statement: Each bucket has a low base fill rate (~10/hr) and a resource cap; an engineering schematic later lets you expand the cap.

creator: nocturne
statement: With expand on, a full bar eats half the resource and raises the cap (100 to 50, new cap 150), expanding each time you fill it.

creator: nocturne
statement: Spend gravel on opals: give X gravel and get an opal, with the gravel cost rising for each next opal.

creator: nocturne
statement: Well opals are how you generate the early opals needed to level Explorer and Engineer; he is at 12 and the next costs about 22 billion.

creator: nocturne
statement: Each bucket fills individually and you can select the rock per bucket; his six buckets make about 2.3-2.4 billion rocks per hour.

creator: nocturne
statement: Use 'remove rock layer' to fill the bucket and unlock the next rock; order is gravel, gold dust, Redstone, mithril and on up to 10.

creator: nocturne
statement: Each layer costs far more; keep unlocking layers, and a layer in 5-6 hours is worth it but don't spend a full day on one.

creator: nocturne
statement: More unlocked rocks means more expansions and so a higher fill-rate multiplier; buckets can all be the same or different rocks.

creator: nocturne
statement: Optimal is expanding all your bars relatively equally until you reach the sixth measurer bonus.

creator: nocturne
statement: After the sixth measurer bonus you need lots of Brunknite ore to upgrade bucket fill rate; engineer upgrades need various ores so expect to mine other ores.

creator: nocturne
statement: After the sixth measurer bonus you need lots of Brunknite ore to upgrade bucket fill rate; engineer upgrades need various ores so expect to mine other ores.

creator: nocturne
statement: There are four ways to boost cavern 1: two from the surface (engineer and measurer) and two from other caverns; everything in the hole interlocks.

creator: nocturne
statement: Engineer schematics boost bucket fill rate; Better Buckets multiplies base by 50%, 10 to 15 per hour.

creator: nocturne
statement: Loading Some Load gives bucket fill rate based on motherload ore mined in cavern 2.

creator: nocturne
statement: Don't spend too much time on motherload ore for bucket fill; other sources are much more significant; just keep unlocking layers.

creator: nocturne
statement: Hunting the Hounds gives bucket fill rate based on hounds killed per class in cavern 3; his kills give 151 per hour.

creator: nocturne
statement: Bar Expanderorama: expanding by eating half the resource raises the total collected and the expansion bonus at the bottom.

creator: nocturne
statement: Unlock the second bucket as soon as you can; it is a huge upgrade that doubles bucket fill rate and lets buckets use different rocks.

creator: nocturne
statement: Motherload and Bucket Synergy gives all buckets +10% per motherload layer unlocked; at about 19-20 layers he gets a 6x multiplier.

creator: nocturne
statement: Unlocking more motherload layers is better for bucket fill rate than having a lot of ore mined.

creator: nocturne
statement: Expander Extravaganza gives all buckets 20% more fill rate based on how many times you've expanded all rocks in the well; more expansions means a bigger bonus.

creator: nocturne
statement: A later Better Buckets raises base from 15 to 20 per hour; the third bucket schematic gives damage based on gold dust, a side note.

creator: nocturne
statement: He has six buckets, the latest unlocked at engineering level 14, and still gets bonuses to the well.

creator: nocturne
statement: Measurer level 6 gives bucket fill based on Brunknite levels, multiplied by your highest single-hit damage (see taskboard Road to Max Damage in world 2).

creator: nocturne
statement: His base rate is about 2400 and the damage multiplier is huge (~8.56 million percent), one of the biggest bucket fill multipliers.

creator: nocturne
statement: Cavern 4 monument bonuses that are bucket fill rate multiply it, almost 16x for him; even a few levels help a lot.

creator: nocturne
statement: Cavern 5 bell ringing can randomly give a bucket fill rate bonus; his is about a 7x multiplier (7140%).

creator: nocturne
statement: Monument and bell multipliers multiply each other so protect them; some mechanics reset the monument and bell.

creator: nocturne
statement: Cavern 2 motherload is the second layer to unlock and is quick; it is where you unlock the Engineer villager.

creator: nocturne
statement: Motherload is an early opal source that slows quickly; it depends on mining efficiency, so warrior classes especially Divine Knights are best.

creator: nocturne
statement: Mining on a character (offline or AFK) reduces a layer's ore; destroy it for one opal, then required mining efficiency rises (638 million for him).

creator: nocturne
statement: You blow through the first five layers fast then get maybe one or two layers per day depending on mining efficiency.

creator: nocturne
statement: Higher mining efficiency and AFK gains from outside the hole make layers easier; he now needs four or five days per layer.

creator: nocturne
statement: Engineer bonuses give bucket fill by layers destroyed and ore mined; use your best mining character to unlock layers fast, which helps Opal exp too.

creator: nocturne
statement: With high AFK gain (possibly 600%) the motherload is faster offline; check back every few minutes for early layers rather than swinging online.

creator: nocturne
statement: After claiming AFK gains the ore drops on the ground and must be picked up to count; don't switch characters too fast or lose 20 hours.

creator: nocturne
statement: Some bonuses give skill efficiency and exp based on motherload layers destroyed which helps destroy more layers; the fractal fly in cavern 8 gives similar skill efficiency.

creator: nocturne
statement: Cavern 3 Dog Den is combat: bring best equipment and talent and card setups for damage accuracy and defense.

creator: nocturne
statement: Dog Den is a wave mechanic where killing more dogs gives more score; it gives many opals early, scaling with your stats.

creator: nocturne
statement: You fight dogs for score and engineer amplifiers multiply score, but each has a penalty; some people are over a million score.

creator: nocturne
statement: The first amplifier raises hounds' base attack; defense and food help survive, and dying ends the run, so find a survivable balance.

creator: nocturne
statement: Don't run prayers that reduce health, accuracy or defense in the Dog Den; the big beefy prayer hinders progress.

creator: nocturne
statement: Don't run prayers that reduce health, accuracy or defense in the Dog Den; the big beefy prayer hinders progress.

creator: nocturne
statement: Base attack amplifier goes to level 100 where dogs deal 418 trillion more damage and mobs one-shot you.

creator: nocturne
statement: Level 100 is impossible for him to survive, but if you kill fast enough you may manage; early dogs give few points, later waves more.

creator: nocturne
statement: The accuracy amplifier needs a set accuracy for 100% hit chance (starts at 6K and stacks quickly); the Shaky bubble in alchemy becomes more useful.

creator: nocturne
statement: The accuracy amplifier needs a set accuracy for 100% hit chance (starts at 6K and stacks quickly); the Shaky bubble in alchemy becomes more useful.

creator: nocturne
statement: Level 100 needs 101 Q accuracy for 100% hit chance; he has 27 trillion so can reach about level 65-70, and may need more accuracy points.

creator: nocturne
statement: Click and hold an amplifier to reset its level so you can reassign levels.

creator: nocturne
statement: Unattacked hounds generate fear (skull bar) and a full bar ends the run; you must kill them quickly and not get one-shot.

creator: nocturne
statement: You need two types of runs; the score run finds the amplifier balance that survives enough waves for highest score and more opals.

creator: nocturne
statement: The kills run matters for the camp engineer bonus giving bucket fill per hounds defeated on best run per class; he has 400 kills on three classes and 200 on beginner.

creator: nocturne
statement: Do a kills run with no amplifiers once per class to get the bonus, plus many score runs to get the highest score.

creator: nocturne
statement: Cavern 4 Monument of Bravery is an AFK mechanic; every 20 hours you play 'tell me a story', a text-based wave fight, for bonuses.

creator: nocturne
statement: Each opal obtained from the monument halves the chance of the next; he has only six, and each killed monster gives a bonus.

creator: nocturne
statement: Bonuses include bucket fill rate, mining efficiency, cooking speed, villager exp, gaming bits, damage and Bell ping rate; higher waves unlock rarer bonuses.

creator: nocturne
statement: Bonus priority: opal ticket first, then Bell ping rate if available, then bucket fill rate and villager exp, then the rest.

creator: nocturne
statement: Priorities depend on your account stage; if you need something like gaming bits, take it instead since you can fight every 20 hours.

creator: nocturne
statement: AFK hours at the monument unlock bonuses on the left side, from 20 to 100, 300, 750 up to 24,000 total hours.

creator: nocturne
statement: AFK hour bonuses only affect the text fight, not the multipliers on the right side as far as he has seen.

creator: nocturne
statement: Waiting beyond 20 hours stacks a reward multiplier (currently 1.6, +60% to bonuses), but opals are never multiplied.

creator: nocturne
statement: He usually gets about 2.3x at the 24-hour mark, roughly once a day unless you use gem shop lamps to speed it up.

creator: nocturne

creator: nocturne
statement: Engineer bonus 'story changes over time': bravery swords get +1 minimum and +10 maximum damage per AFK hour at the monument.

creator: nocturne
statement: First Try I Swear: throwing the last sword first and one-shotting the mob gives a damage bonus, but if you don't one-shot it you lose it.

creator: nocturne
statement: Throw the last sword first enough times to kill successfully then stop to keep the damage bonus; it's a gamble and RNG can't be fixed.

creator: nocturne
statement: Reroll Keeper: rerolling a sword throw resets mob HP so you can rethrow for a higher roll; not using rerolls gives a damage multiplier.

creator: nocturne
statement: Each unused reroll gives 10% damage, so using none gives 50%; his swords deal 272 to 57,000 before bonuses.

creator: nocturne
statement: Further bonuses give two extra swords, rethrow up to five swords per day, and one more sword; base is three swords and he has six.

creator: nocturne
statement: If you fail a fight you lose all bonuses collected since your last failure, so avoid gambling and losing them.

creator: nocturne
statement: The only way to keep bonuses is to run away; swords need not be used in order, and the Last Sword gives a bonus.

creator: nocturne
statement: One-shotting with the last sword gave a 10% damage buff; he prioritizes bucket fill rate when choosing a bonus for clearing a round.

creator: nocturne
statement: A higher max damage makes a kill more likely, but you can still roll the minimum 272 and lose the bonus.

creator: nocturne
statement: Upgrading the measurer raises the sword's maximum damage; bucket fill rate is a higher priority than village exp.

creator: nocturne
statement: Priority: opals always first then bucket fill rate or Bell ping if the wave allows it then village exp then the rest.

creator: nocturne
statement: Be cautious with the bonus increasing opal chance from the monument since each opal gives a 50% penalty; heavy levels may not be worth it.

creator: nocturne
statement: He only risks the last-sword gamble on mobs around 10-15k HP at his damage so he can kill more waves later.

creator: nocturne
statement: The gamble threshold depends on each person's comfort and damage, and he can't give a universal answer.

creator: nocturne
statement: Don't use rethrows unless needed because unused rethrows give the 50% damage multiplier; a rethrow resets HP and respins the throw.

creator: nocturne
statement: He spends a rethrow when a roll is too low (9,000) since he needs at least 40,000 to do 200,000 total.

creator: nocturne
statement: After a rethrow he got 25,000 more damage to kill one more wave; killing 270,000 HP is a huge gamble.

creator: nocturne
statement: He rethrows a poor 172k roll and wins at 110k; if he loses he gets the bonuses back tomorrow.

creator: nocturne
statement: Each rethrow used is permanently gone, and you can't use a banked rethrow on your last sword if you die, so don't save one for it.

creator: nocturne
statement: Take the last level up and run away to bank the levels; losing a fight loses collected bonuses and listed right-side bonuses needing days to rebuild.

creator: nocturne
statement: As damage and engineer/measurer multipliers grow you clear more waves; don't take big risks, keeping bucket fill rate and bonuses matters more than one more level.

creator: nocturne
statement: Cavern 5 Bell has four sections plus engineer and measurer bonuses; ringing the bell generates bell power hourly to spend.

creator: nocturne
statement: Each ring gives a random level in bucket fill rate, harp note gains (cavern 6), villager exp or daily lamp wishes (cavern 7); engineer bonuses give multiple levels.

creator: nocturne
statement: His ring gave +20% bucket fill rate; he makes 2.3 million per hour, and each ring raises the next cost, so a ring takes hours.

creator: nocturne
statement: Pinging the Bell is the opal mechanic; ring, ping and clean are separate resources and you pick one to generate at a time.

creator: nocturne
statement: His ping is 584,000 per hour needing 9.2 million per opal; opals never reset when you renew the bell.

statement: With oxidizing layer you eventually unlock improvements after a few fails; spending 8,000 clean per second for the sixth isn't worth it now but will be later.
